primary.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
primary.sections: Section 2.1.2, Example 2.15, with the constant-step branch of Theorem 2.13

notation.meaning: For r=<z,x>-y, H_delta(r)=r^2/2 when |r|<=delta and delta(|r|-delta/2) otherwise. The convex regularity claims make the source-implicit convention delta>=0 explicit. At delta=0 the loss is zero; negative thresholds are outside those claims.

The source uses R^d; the Lean chain works in a complete real inner-product space. Predictors and comparators range over the full space. Features z_t are known before prediction; labels y_t enter the next update. The deterministic theorem assumes a feature norm bound but no label, residual or predictor bound.
R_T(u) sums ell_t(X_t)-ell_t(u) for t=0,...,T-1. X_0 is the source first predictor x_1, and X_T is source x_(T+1). The comparator u is fixed throughout a run.

At each T>0 choose eta_T=1/sqrt(T), one constant step for that whole run. Coefficient one specializes the source proportionality prescription. The initial state, threshold, feature bound and comparator stay fixed as T varies. Eventual cutoffs may depend on the comparator and epsilon.

steps.title: Predict before feedback
steps.detail: The current point depends only on strict-prefix losses. Current feature z_t is available before predicting inner(z_t,x_t); then y_t is revealed and defines the current residual/loss. Library index0 is source round1, and iterate T is the source point after T updates.

steps.title: Compute the true Huber gradient
steps.detail: Actual seam calculus produces the scalar derivative, including both seams and delta0. The ambient inner-product chain rule then produces gradient H_delta'(inner(z_t,x)-y_t)*z_t and norm<=delta*norm(z_t); no supplied desired-gradient, label/residual bound or regularity oracle.

steps.title: Update in the full space
steps.detail: The genuine nonempty/closed/convex fullSpace Domain has selected projection identity. Global convexity and differentiability PRODUCE RegularLoss fullSpace, discharging the stronger historical API globally. Subtract eta times the current gradient for the next point in the same shared causal recursion; no finite diameter or bounded predictor set.

source_theorems.label: Example 2.15: Huber prediction, with a derived quantitative bound
source_theorems.fallback: Only the numeric upper envelope tends0. For each fixed predictor u and epsilon>0, actual average regret is eventually <epsilon; it may stay negative.
source_theorems.plain: Bounded features give bounded Huber gradients on the full predictor space. Constant-step OGD then gives a one-sided average-performance guarantee against each fixed linear predictor.
source_theorems.relationship: The example prints the piecewise loss and gradient, asserts convexity, and applies Theorem 2.13 with a step proportional to 1/sqrt(T). The displayed coefficient-one bound is derived, not a verbatim source formula. Scalar seam calculus fills an omitted source proof. The complete real inner-product-space formulation generalizes finite Euclidean vectors; delta>=0 makes the intended threshold convention explicit. The informal average-performance sentence is represented by eventual upper inequalities, without claiming an existing signed limit or equality to zero.

steps.title: Join the scalar pieces
steps.detail: At residuals plus and minus delta, adjacent values and derivatives agree. Gluing the three formulas gives the clamp derivative, whose monotonicity proves convexity. This includes the coincident seams at delta=0.
steps.fallback: The generic gluing lemmas are internal calculus support. Convexity and derivative bounds are produced from the literal loss, not supplied as caller assumptions.

steps.title: Differentiate the feature residual
steps.detail: Compose with x maps to <z_t,x>-y_t. The inner-product chain rule produces the gradient, and scalar derivative bounds control its norm for every predictor. Affine composition gives global convexity and differentiability.
steps.fallback: No restriction on labels, residuals or predictors is needed. The proof supplies the global RegularLoss bundle required by the shared OGD API.

steps.title: Use the actual full-space update
steps.detail: Projection onto the full space is the identity. The shared recurrence therefore subtracts eta times the actual gradient after each label is revealed. Applying the positive constant-step theorem and the feature bound retains the terminal distance, including its cancellation at horizon zero.
steps.fallback: The parent is theorem_2_13_fixed. The bounded-diameter DLsqrt(T) specialization is not used on this unbounded domain.

steps.title: Tune a separate run for each horizon
steps.detail: For T>0, choose eta_T=1/sqrt(T), discard the nonpositive terminal term and divide by T. The threshold, feature bound, initial state and fixed comparator determine a finite numerator independent of T.
steps.fallback: The superscript records a horizon-indexed family of constant-step runs. This is not an anytime step eta_t.

steps.title: Read the terminal inequality precisely
steps.detail: The numerical envelope tends to zero. For each fixed comparator and epsilon>0 it is eventually below epsilon, hence so is the actual signed average regret. This argument supplies no lower bound and does not prove that signed average regret converges to zero.
steps.fallback: The conclusion is the literal eventual inequality. No real-valued limsup theorem, uniform cutoff over unbounded comparators, absolute convergence or financial accuracy statement is claimed.

notation.meaning: For r=<z,x>-y, H_delta(r)=r^2/2 when |r|<=delta and delta(|r|-delta/2) otherwise. The convex regularity claims make the source-implicit convention delta>=0 explicit. At delta=0 the loss is zero; negative thresholds are outside those claims.

R_T(u) sums ell_t(X_t)-ell_t(u) for t=0,...,T-1. X_0 is the source first predictor x_1, and X_T is source x_(T+1). The comparator u is fixed throughout a run.
